symptom: A custom error handler that falls through (`on error without rollback begin log …; end error;`, no RETURN/RAISE ERROR) on an activity inside an IF branch was wired to the wrong place. With a result variable (`$N = call microflow …`, `$Obj = create …`, `$R = call rest service … returns response`) the handler's last activity flowed into a merge spliced in FRONT of the enclosing split — an endless loop while the call kept failing (runtime: 3063 'failed' lines in ~5s, after-startup never returned); describe printed `merge rejoin1;` before the if and `join rejoin1;` in the handler. Without one it flowed into a new end event (describe: a `return;` in the handler the source never had) — nothing after the failure ran; with `returns Boolean as $Result` that end returned the non-existent $Result (CE0109, the only shape any check caught). Same in IF/ELSE (either arm), CASE and type-split arms, nanoflow loop/while bodies and `while true`; in a THEN that ends in RETURN the handler skipped to the code after the IF. check, exec and mx check passed (ako/mxcli#1459, mendixlabs/mxcli#1565)
cause: Pending fall-through rejoins live in one builder-wide slot (errorHandlerSource/TailFrom/SkipVar + queue) that only buildFlowGraph's top-level loop settled, on the flow LEAVING the failing activity. The branch body loops (addIfStatement ×3, addEnumSplit, addStructuredInheritanceSplit, the loop/while sub-builders, addManualWhileTrueStatement) settled only an EMPTY handler (`emptyErrorHandlerFrom == lastID`), so a non-empty one leaked out of the branch and the enclosing loop settled it on the next flow it drew: the skip-var path (taken whenever the activity has an output variable) ignores the origin and spliced it into `previous -> split`; without skipVar nothing matched and terminatePendingErrorHandlersAtEnd gave it an end event; inside a loop sub-builder it was simply dropped (no outgoing flow = iteration ends)
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_flows.go` (enterBranch/leaveBranch/settleBranchFlow, pendingHandlers; mergeOnEdge keeps a branch-exit rejoin merge on the branch row), `cmd_microflows_builder_control.go` (addIfStatement: per-arm scope, settle every in-arm flow and the arm's exit into the merge, merge created lazily when a returning arm leaves a handler; loop/while/while-true bodies), `cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go` (addEnumSplit, addStructuredInheritanceSplit)
insight: Scope the pending-handler slot to each branch body (take it on entry, hand back only what the branch could not settle) instead of adding an origin guard to the skip-var path: the skip-var delay exists precisely so a rejoin can land on a flow whose origin is NOT the source, and the shared slot also let an in-branch flow settle the ENCLOSING path's handler. The 'third shape' (handler in a THEN ending in RETURN joining the IF's exit merge) was a30881bbb's deliberate shared continuation; it is kept only where it was earned — a skip-var handler whose next statement reads the failed output — and the merge is now created only when a returning arm actually leaves one (static bodyHasContinuingCustomErrorHandler over-predicted it). Assert on the graph (where does the handler's last activity go next, through merges) with a control that the failing activity's own next is the same node; describe text alone misleads because the broken loop-body shape describes as a clean fall-through. Runtime A/B on 11.12.2 (after-startup, parseInteger('x') callee): fixed = before/failed/after call/end once each. A custom handler inside a MICROFLOW loop is CE0644 regardless, so the loop part matters for nanoflows. Not the same root cause as ako/mxcli#1455 (handler-body loop drops the deferred false case on in-body flows)
